concepts.label: managed-object
concepts.gloss: A managed-object representing a monitored compute resource (physical server, VM, or container) that is the subject of events, alarms and clears in the fault system.
concepts.example: node-14 — the physical server 'node-14' being monitored (it is the owner of events like 'trap-cpu-node14-t0' and alarms like 'alarm-node14-overtemp').

concepts.label: event
concepts.gloss: A discrete incoming notification (syslog/trap/SNMP trap) that reports an observed occurrence on a specific managed node and serves as raw input to fault processing.
concepts.example: trap-cpu-node14-t0 — a CPU temperature trap emitted for node-14 at time t0 indicating an observed high CPU/thermal condition.

concepts.label: alarm
concepts.gloss: An active alarm condition raised for a particular managed node that carries structured attributes describing its perceived severity and a standardized probable-cause code.
concepts.example: alarm-node14-overtemp — an active over-temperature alarm on node-14 which carries a severity (e.g., 'critical') and a probable-cause (e.g., 'thermalTrip').

concepts.label: severity
concepts.gloss: A categorical perceived-severity label attached to an alarm that indicates the operational impact level (examples: critical, major, minor, warning).
concepts.example: critical — the perceived-severity value assigned to 'alarm-node14-overtemp' to denote highest impact on service/operation.

concepts.label: probable-cause
concepts.gloss: A standardized cause-code (X.733 style) carried by an alarm that identifies the likely root cause or triggering condition of the fault.
concepts.example: thermalTrip — the probable-cause code attached to 'alarm-node14-overtemp' indicating the fault was triggered by a thermal trip event.

concepts.label: clear
concepts.gloss: A clear notification that explicitly clears or resolves a previously raised alarm on a managed node, referencing the alarm it clears.
concepts.example: clear-alarm-node14-overtemp — a clear message indicating that the 'alarm-node14-overtemp' condition on node-14 has been acknowledged/resolved and should be cleared.
